key_insight: AtomWorld-Mirror replaces slow atom-by-atom replay with macro-step transitions that predict both structural changes and elapsed physical time, enabling much faster long-horizon materials evolution modeling.
engineering_relevance: This could accelerate atomic-scale simulation workflows for materials design and reliability studies by making long-term evolution tractable without fully simulating every micro-event.
method: Distills short micro-event segments into reachable macro transitions between key atomic states
Jointly predicts sparse structural edits and accumulated physical time in latent dynamics
Uses physical constraints for local reachability, inventory conservation, and continuous-time consistency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across five atomic systems, including irradiation aging, metallic glass, and solid electrolyte cases, with 10^3 to 10^4× speedups over event-by-event simulation.
watch_item: Macro-step predictions may depend on the quality of key-state selection and constraint enforcement, so failures could occur if rare local events are not well captured.
paper_title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics
